on_r_the_big_gulp.blurb: The Big Gulp is the most northerly sector of the Mount Nemo cliff near Burlington, a single line of Niagara Escarpment dolomite broken by gullies. It holds about twenty routes, a little over half of them trad and the rest bolted sport lines. The range is wide: a handful of very easy lines, a solid middle band of 5.6 to 5.9, and a few steeper sport leads from 5.10 up to 5.12. That mix makes it a reasonable stop for a mixed party where one climber wants gentle trad and another wants harder bolted pitches. Reaching it means a walk along the cliff-top trail and a scramble down a gully to the base.

on_slippery_people_area.blurb: Slippery People Area is a sector of Devil's Glen, an escarpment limestone cliff in Ontario's Grey County that is known for many of the province's classic lines. Roughly twenty routes are spread along the wall, around half bolted and the rest trad. Most of the climbing sits between 5.9 and 5.13, with a particularly dense cluster at 5.10 and 5.11, plus a couple of easier pitches and a few at the top of the range. The cliff is long and faces south, so it takes sun for much of the day, though the glen itself can feel shaded and secluded. Weekends bring crowds, and biting insects are heavy in early summer.

on_golf_town.blurb: Golf Town is a small dolomite sector at the far northern end of Metcalfe Rock, the escarpment cliff above Grey Road 19 near Collingwood. About twenty routes are packed in here, most of them bolted sport lines with a few trad options, and many carry golf-themed names. Grades run from a very easy line up to 5.12, but the bulk fall between 5.8 and 5.11, so it suits climbers who are comfortable on intermediate sport. The wall is shaded and tree-covered, which keeps it cooler on hot days and slower to dry after rain. Metcalfe is quiet midweek and busier on weekends.

on_long_wall_right.blurb: Long Wall Right is the biggest sector of Claghorn, a remote cliff roughly an hour's drive from Thunder Bay in northwestern Ontario. The cliffs there average around 30 metres and the setting is secluded, so expect a quiet day with a long walk in. About twenty routes are split almost evenly between trad and sport. The grades are demanding: one 5.8 and one 5.9, then the bulk of the wall from 5.10 through 5.12, with a few lines at 5.13. This is a place for confident leaders rather than beginners.
